title: 1.4 Quantity of heat II: measuring latent heat and cooling curves

1.title: Question: the electrical method for ice

q.Q1: Q1. A 50 W heater runs for 300 s. 60 g of ice melts in the heater funnel and 15 g in the control funnel. Calculate the specific latent heat of fusion.

q.Q2: Q2. 20 g of ice at 0 °C is added to 200 g of water at 30 °C; the final temperature is 21 °C. Find L for ice (c water = 4200 J/kg/K; ignore the calorimeter).
q.Q3: Q3. Why is this answer lower than the accepted value of 3.34 × 10^5 J/kg?

q.Q4: Q4. A 1000 W kettle boils off 0.12 kg of water in 5 minutes once boiling. Estimate L_v and give one reason the value may be too high.

q.Q5: Q5. Explain why food cooks faster in a pressure cooker.
q.Q6: Q6. Explain why the cooling curve of molten wax has a flat section.

q.Q7: Q7. How much heat is needed to change 0.05 kg of ice at −10 °C to steam at 100 °C? (c ice 2100, c water 4200 J/kg/K; Lf 3.34 × 10^5, Lv 2.26 × 10^6 J/kg)
